backbone: Integer solvability reduces to an effective family of finite rational-solvability tests; compactness plus elliptic and abelian-surface height bounds show all tests succeeding forces an integer zero.
quote: If a rational-solvability algorithm existed, we could run two searches in parallel: enumeration of integer zeros, and enumeration of tests until one fails.
reason: Headline proof closes with a height contradiction; inputs are height bounds and sieve estimates (E1). Compactness/model theory and modularity are supporting, so E4, E6 secondary.

backbone: Unfold packet measures into weighted ideal counts; Stark and Shiu bounds give nonescape and small-ball bounds, hence positive entropy, so measure rigidity identifies every weak limit as Haar.
quote: packet averages of lattice-vector counts control the cusp and small ordinary balls, and these bounds feed into positive-entropy rigidity.
reason: Scaling-limit convention: nonescape of mass (tightness) plus rigidity identifying every weak limit as Haar gives F5 primary, F1 secondary.

backbone: Induction on dimension from known low-dimensional and fourfold cases: stable degeneration to a K-polystable cone, stabilizer and jet-cone estimates force smooth Gorenstein cone, then quadric characterization.
quote: Starting from the known cases in dimensions two and three and the fourfold companion, we argue by induction.
reason: Backbone is degeneration to K-polystable cones, stabilizers, Gorenstein semigroups and quadric characterization: structural algebraic geometry (E4); the jet and slice estimates are E1 secondary.

backbone: Explicitly build a rank-two bundle G glued along three graphs; quotient sequences prove ampleness, while a Griffiths-positive metric would yield a quadratic limit and incompatible invariant measures.
quote: We construct $G$ together with two line-bundle quotients. Their dual inclusions will span away from three graphs and agree on those graphs through specified linear maps.
reason: Bundle glued along three graphs plus the invariant-measure obstruction (incompatible invariances under power and Mobius maps) are geometric/dynamical (E5); psh estimates E1, exact sequences E4 secondary.

backbone: On a maximal-Betti cover the Albanese fibre group N is FAb; if N were infinite, a minimal base and L2-Dolbeault/Hilbert-tensor arguments give a Bogomolov sheaf, contradicting specialness.
quote: It remains to exclude infinite \(N\); a finite kernel of a lattice quotient gives virtual abelianity by elementary group theory.
reason: Core machinery is L2-Dolbeault cohomology with Hilbert coefficients, positivity descent and a Bogomolov sheaf (sheaf/cohomological, E4); fibration and cover geometry E5 secondary.

backbone: Via Chen's equivalence, reduce bounded klt complements to a birational lct lower bound, proved by contradiction along a sequence using constrained normalized-volume minimization, residual towers and uniform estimates.
quote: We formulate it in Proposition~\ref{prop:birational-threshold} and prove it by contradiction.
reason: Valuations, constrained normalized-volume minimizers, filtrations, torus quotients and residual towers are structural birational geometry (E4); uniform estimates are E1 secondary. Consistent with 037.

backbone: Reduce a.e. convergence to a good-set integral bound for bounded-height inputs summed over layers; prove it by a finite dyadic procedure with budgets, stopping rules and entropy-compression refinements.
quote: For positive input, apply the finite procedure of \Cref{sec:procedure}, with the common stopping rule in the statement.
reason: Rule 5: the reduction to the good-set estimate is short; the bulk and organizing idea is the finite dyadic procedure with budgets and stopping rules (iteration with stopping argument), so F3, F1 secondary.

backbone: Randomly construct cut families on a column model of the planar graph by multiscale local updates; every outcome gives the upper bound, random changes give the lower bound.
quote: We construct two families of measurable label sets, denoted by $\mathcal A_v$ and $\mathcal B_v$ at a point $v$.
reason: Steps live on a geometric column model of the planar graph (bands, portals, radial cells, ordered arcs, distance fields): E5; probability/Lipschitz estimates E1 and combinatorics E3 secondary.

backbone: Explicitly construct a multiscale doubling subset of l2; a lexicographic extremal-derivative energy estimate plus crossings forces a packing contradiction for any bi-Lipschitz map into R^k.
quote: There is a fixed subset $S$ of real $\ell_2$, equipped with its induced Hilbert distance, whose doubling constant is at most $76800$ and which admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into $\R^k$
reason: Paper: 'the analytic step uses ordinary Euclidean differentiation ... and a quadratic variance identity'; the anisotropic energy estimates drive the nonembedding (E1); the strip geometry is E5 secondary.

backbone: Explicit graph reduction from perfect-completeness Label Cover; a large independent set is decoded to bounded label lists, aligned via minimax and Ramsey, then a coefficient test gives soundness.
quote: there is a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm $R_\delta$ that maps each explicitly encoded Boolean $3$-CNF formula $\phi$ to a nonempty finite simple undirected unweighted graph $G_\phi$
reason: Soundness analysis (juntas for the sup metric, coefficient test with rotation experiments, expected-square bounds) is analytic/probabilistic (E1); gadget graph and Ramsey/minimax are E3 secondary.

backbone: Rank measure from differentiation and multiplication: homogeneous depth-five circuits of size S have small measure, trace-moment computation shows IMM has large measure, compare; block expansion gives upper bound.
quote: Let $K$ be a field, and let $g\in K[V,U]$ be a homogeneous degree-$n$ polynomial computed by a syntactically homogeneous $\Sigma\Pi\Sigma\Pi\Sigma$ circuit of size $S$. Then \[ R(g)\le 2S^2D\exp(C\sqrt n)\,n^{-\sqrt n/100}. \]
reason: Both halves are asymptotic bounds on a rank measure (binomial-ratio and path-type sum estimates, n^{-sqrt n/100} vs exp(-C sqrt n)); E1 primary, exact trace computation E2 and path counting E3 secondary.

backbone: Build the diffeomorphism as a smooth limit of stages, each perturbation letting Koopman Laurent polynomials of f approximate a further test function, so iterates of f span L2_0.
quote: In every prescribed neighborhood of $S$ there is an admissible pair $(S',f')$, with good arc $I'$, and a finite Laurent polynomial $P$ such that
reason: Rule 5: the diffeomorphism is a smooth limit of stages and the paper presents the stage iteration, not the object, first, so F3 primary with F4 (and F5 limit) secondary.

backbone: Take the least dimension where the bound fails; polynomial interpolation on selected direction stars, secant/variety degree bounds and rigid-motion incidence (Guth-Katz input) yield a contradiction.
quote: Suppose that Theorem~\ref{thm:main} fails, and take the least dimension \(d\ge3\) in which it fails.
reason: Contradiction is reached through polynomial interpolation, variety degrees, secants, projections and skew-form flat incidences: algebro-geometric incidence geometry (E5); graph selection/counting E3 secondary.

backbone: Reduce to partitioning dual triangulation vertices into two induced trees; a nonvanishing weighted exponential sum over state pairs forces a forest pair, with induction over separating triangles.
quote: These contributions cannot cancel. Some pair with \(Q_s\) a forest must remain.
reason: Paper's strategy and most sections establish a pair of states via a nonvanishing weighted sum ('These contributions cannot cancel'), a non-constructive existence (F5); induction over separating triangles is a short reduction (F3 secondary).

backbone: Commuting division-coefficient forms transfer minimal resolutions; leading coefficient spaces give a monomial ideal with equal Hilbert function and larger Betti numbers; inductive monomial comparison reaches lex-plus-powers.
quote: The essential step is to find a monomial ideal \(M\supseteq P\) such that
reason: J is prescribed by the statement, not built in the proof; the headline is a Betti comparison obtained by chaining beta(I)<=beta(M)<=beta(J). The auxiliary monomial ideal M is F4 secondary, so F1 primary.

backbone: After a unimodular reduction, amplified endpoint maps give critical moment bounds, then a subpower triangle bound, and corridor deformation gives a spectral contradiction bounding the critical operator norm.
quote: If $T_\pc$ were unbounded, sprinkling would imply $\norm{T_p}\ge c(\pc-p)^{-1}$. ... This contradiction proves critical boundedness.
reason: Tex proof strategy: both main steps argue by contradiction (assumed divergent moment; T_pc unbounded). Convention: assume-and-derive-impossibility stays F2 even when the impossibility is quantitative.

backbone: Exact circuit orthogonality identities plus endpoint transport give a discrete observable whose subsequential limits are holomorphic with a uniquely solvable boundary problem, identifying every crossing limit as Cardy.
quote: The resulting boundary-value problem has the conformal map to an equilateral triangle as its unique solution ... This common boundary problem identifies every subsequential crossing limit.
reason: Scaling-limit convention: precompactness of crossing observables then identification of every subsequential limit by a uniquely solvable boundary problem gives F5 primary, F1 secondary.

backbone: Tightness plus identification of every subsequential limit: reflection positivity, pin motion and boundary comparison yield harmonic moment identities and a Wick recursion, which determine the Gaussian free field.
quote: The main task is to identify every subsequential limit $H$ of the integer height field.
reason: Scaling-limit convention: 'The main task is to identify every subsequential limit'; uniform moment bounds give tightness. Both labellers had F1/F5 reversed; convention puts F5 primary, F1 secondary.

backbone: Take the explicit periodic Steinberg group St_12(R) over a finitely presented matrix-nil graded algebra; phases of long words and homological stability let degree truncations detect all elements.
quote: We construct an infinite group with an ordinary finite presentation in which every element has finite order, answering the finitely presented Burnside question negatively.
reason: Detection of the central Steinberg kernel J(R) (a K_2-type object) and integral homological stability via frame complexes are K-theory/homology (E4); explicit phase and word computations E2 secondary.

backbone: A kernel element yields a planar disk-and-band surface; a multi-block unitary fixed-space theorem and spectral-phase subadditivity show one nontrivial boundary word is impossible, so the coefficient is trivial.
quote: The upper bound forces the extra term to vanish, so this word is trivial.
reason: Principal new tool is the multi-block fixed-space theorem via intersection classes on products of unitary groups, applied on a planar disk-and-band surface: topological (E5); spectral-phase inequality E1, cohomology E4 secondary.

backbone: Bound collar mutual information via spectral-gap norm comparisons on replica operators (bootstrapping a box exponent), then entropy chain rules over ordered region families give the area law.
quote: If each region shares little information with the complement of $A$ together with the earlier regions of its own family, two applications of the entropy chain rule cancel all individual region entropies.
reason: Tex 'How the proof is organized' gives a five-stage forward pipeline (initial exponent, interpolation, norm comparison, amplification, chain-rule cancellation); the exponent bootstrap is one stage, so F1 primary, F3 secondary.

backbone: Construct a total function from Forrelation instances with addressed certificates and pointers; quantum tournament search gives the upper bound, a planted-input direct-product argument gives the randomized lower bound.
quote: We construct a total function whose accepting certificate belongs to one column.
reason: Both analyses are probabilistic estimates: weight-drift tournament bounds for the quantum upper bound and coupled planted-input direct-product bounds for R (E1); pointer-function construction E3, cited Forrelation bounds E6.

backbone: Existing criteria reduce to a core fixed-point equality; the multiplication identity R=L·exp(iX⊗Y), obtained from the absolute bicentralizer theorem and repeated tensor tests (each by contradiction), yields the commutation.
quote: Existing bicentralizer criteria reduce our task to showing that the extension of $\gamma$ to $B\rtimes_{\sigma^\varphi}\R$ has fixed algebra $N'\cap c(M)$.
reason: Headline relative theorem is reduced directly via existing criteria to a fixed-point equality from R=L exp(iX(x)Y); contradictions sit inside lemmas (rule 1, F2 secondary). Core sections are modular-energy estimates and tensor tests (E1).

backbone: Reduce to a faithful central state; on the normalizer part build a random Bernoulli coloring via mixed determinantal polynomials and iterative pinning; elsewhere use random diagonal unitaries.
quote: We construct a measurable coloring there that has uniform conditional color marginals and makes the pinched matrix small on any prescribed finite-radius ball with arbitrarily high probability.
reason: Rule 3: the paving partition comes from a random measurable coloring on a Bernoulli extension and random labels/unitaries, never written down; F5 primary, iterative pinning F3 and the corner reduction F1 secondary.

backbone: A minimal-order counterexample has a Lie-type component in a short list; for each family, frame cycles, dimension estimates and propagation produce nonzero rational homology, a contradiction.
quote: Let $G$ be a minimal-order counterexample to \eqref{eq:HQC} for $p=2$.
reason: The contradiction is produced by building nonzero rational homology classes (frame cycles, boundary cancellation, propagation lemma, products of cycles): homological (E4); explicit Lie-type sign/coefficient computations E2 secondary.

backbone: Construct an explicit presentation with zero twisted H_2 for a character detecting an order-two element, apply a finite plus construction; a cyclic-tower obstruction excludes any finite 2-complex model.
quote: Section~\ref{sec:construction} then gives a five-generator, four-relator presentation and a perfect normal subgroup generated normally by two powers.
reason: Twisted second homology, cellular chain complexes over ZG and its persistence under cyclic covers carry both halves (E4); Fox-calculus computation E2 and the cyclic-tower lifting E5 secondary.

backbone: Run a localized Kahler-Ricci flow, control it by disc-envelope and Harnack inequalities to get shrinking holomorphic charts, then assemble them by complex dynamics into a biholomorphism with C^n.
quote: A second route uses geometric flow to construct shrinking holomorphic charts and then assembles those charts by complex dynamics.
reason: Tex 'Structure of the proof' is a forward chain: flow, disc envelope, Harnack, shrinking charts, polynomial models; inverse iteration is only the final assembly, so F1 primary with F3, F4 secondary.

backbone: Prove a localized Łojasiewicz-type gradient inequality for Gaussian area near the shrinker via a finite-jet obstruction, then propagate it with a bootstrap to finite length and unique convergence.
quote: Gradient inequalities connect small stationary defect to finite length of the rescaled flow.
reason: Most of the paper derives the localized gradient inequality from the finite-jet obstruction; the graph-improvement bootstrap is the closing application, not the organizing idea (rule 5 not met). F1 primary, F3 secondary.

backbone: Layered exact finite expansion of interacting histories over time cells, centered against the Boltzmann solution; history integrals and tree counting with a single energy budget bound remainders, summed to convergence.
quote: Their layered expansion retains the earlier histories of correlated remainders while extracting the factors approximated by the kinetic solution.
reason: Tex 'Structure of the proof' centers on an exact layered expansion, centering identities and history estimates; the chronological induction over layers appears only in the closing summation, so F1 primary, F3 secondary.
